correctness.rationale: Using the standard interval model for Nakayama modules, Frobenius dimension is a sum of n^2 injective-projective Hom dimensions. In the cyclic quasi-hereditary case, a projective-dimension-two simple forces a plateau in the monotone endpoint function; this bounds all Hom dimensions by 2 and forces the unique possible dimension-2 pair to be a projective-injective P_1. The displayed family attains n^2+1.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. The 2020 MathOverflow question explicitly conjectures n^2+1 and still has no answer; targeted searches found no later exact solution. A 2026 paper on Frobenius-dimension bounds is a residual risk because only its abstract and indexed descriptions were inspected, not its full text.

value.rationale: The theorem gives an exact all-n solution to the published extremal question and an explicit extremal family, with a short structural explanation for the n^2+1 formula.
